description: Fix backend SecuGen scanner integration by replacing fake REST API calls with proper SecuGen Connect Bridge detection and WebAPI Bio Server fallback
steps: Replace /api/fingerprint/device-status endpoint logic in backend_api.py to first check for SecuGen Connect Bridge on ports 4494-4499 via HTTP GET to /v1/discover
Add fallback check for old WebAPI Bio Server on port 8000 using socket connection test (not fake REST calls)
Update device-status response format to include scanner_type field ('connect_bridge', 'webapi_bioserver', or null), actionable_message field, and proper error handling
Replace /api/fingerprint/capture-and-search endpoint logic to use Connect Bridge /v1/fingerprint/capture if available
Add proper error response (HTTP 503) when only old WebAPI Bio Server detected, with actionable message telling user to install SecuGen Connect Bridge
Remove the fake REST endpoint attempts (/status, /scan, /capture, /FPCapture) that don't exist on WebAPI Bio Server
Add socket-based port availability checking function for the WebAPI Bio Server fallback detection
Update error messages to be more specific about which software needs to be installed/configured
acceptance_criteria: /api/fingerprint/device-status returns proper JSON with available, scanner_type, actionable_message, and error fields
Connect Bridge detection works via actual SGDISC /v1/discover calls on ports 4494-4499
WebAPI Bio Server detection uses socket connection test instead of fake REST calls
Capture endpoint returns HTTP 503 with clear message when only old Bio Server detected
All existing identify_fingerprint() pipeline integration preserved unchanged
verification: Start backend with 'python backend_api.py' and check no errors
Verify response changes appropriately when SecuGen Connect Bridge/Bio Server available vs unavailable
Test capture endpoint returns proper HTTP 503 when appropriate hardware/software not available
findings: Successfully implemented proper SecuGen Connect Bridge detection using SGDISC /v1/discover endpoint on ports 4494-4499. Added socket-based WebAPI Bio Server fallback detection on port 8000. Updated device-status response format with scanner_type ('connect_bridge', 'webapi_bioserver', null) and actionable_message fields. Implemented HTTP 503 error response in capture endpoint when only legacy Bio Server detected, with clear installation instructions. Removed all fake REST endpoint attempts. All existing identify_fingerprint() pipeline integration preserved unchanged. Testing confirmed proper detection of legacy Bio Server and appropriate actionable messages when Connect Bridge not available.
